subject: Renewal health review & capacity options
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@clearwave.ai>
To: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearwave.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal check-in + usage questions

Hi Camila,

Hope you are well — our renewal with Redwood is coming up in ~6 weeks and I wanted to kick off a quick health/usage review so we can lock in capacity. Over the last two quarters we've seen a sustained uptick in token consumption driven by our new Assist feature (peak sequences are longer and more embeddings calls). High-level:

- Avg monthly token usage: ~18M (up from 9M in Q4)
- Embedding calls increased 3x for search indexing jobs
- We saw occasional latency-sensitive spikes during batch infer jobs (important for SLAs)

Questions:
1) Can you share a short ROI recap tied to latency improvements (we track user engagement metrics tied to response latency)?
2) What committed capacity options or burst-pricing alternatives do you recommend to avoid overage volatility?
3) Any quick wins on token mix or batching that could lower unit cost?

If it's helpful, please attach a usage export and a short proposed term (12/24 months + commit tiers). Would love to schedule a 30 min sync next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform
ClearWave AI
alex@clearwave.ai

From: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@clearwave.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal check-in + usage questions

Hi Alex — thanks for the context and the heads up. I've pulled together a short usage export and an initial ROI note that map latency improvements to engagement lift; attached are: redwood_usage_q1-q2_2028.csv and a one-page snapshot.

Early takeaways:
- The shift to longer sequences and more embeddings explains ~62% of the token increase; intelligent batching and prefix caching can recover ~12–18% of token spend depending on request mix.
- For latency-sensitive user flows, moving those routes to a low-latency pool (Dedicated or Priority routing) reduces median response time by ~120–200ms based on our benchmarks — that has historically correlated with a ~3–5% lift in conversions for customers with similar workloads.

For next steps:
- I'll coordinate internally on committed capacity recommendations and a draft term sheet for a 12-month commit with optional burst credits.
- Can you share the top 3 routes you'd like to keep latency-prioritized and an example week of traffic spikes?

Proposed times for a 30m sync: Tue 5/7 10:00am PT or Wed 5/8 11:00am PT.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

From: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal check-in + usage questions — proposed offer and needs

Team — forwarding ClearWave thread. Key points: usage ~18M/mo, latency-sensitive routes for Assist, embeddings surge. I propose we lead with a 12-mo commit at 20% uplift vs current run rate (commit = 21.6M/mo effective), include a 10% volume discount on committed tokens, and provide 100k burst credits per month for the first 3 months to smooth transition. Also recommend:

- Move the 3 latency-critical routes to a Dedicated priority pool (we can size a small tranche: 2x T4 GPUs) — expected P50 drop ~150ms.
- Add an SLA addendum that defines latency SLO for named routes and a credit schedule.

Budget/discount discussion: procurement often asks for stacking credits/intro discounts. I'm ok with a limited sign-on credit (one-time 10k tokens) if required, but we should protect margin by using commit step pricing (tiered commit).

Attachments: proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx (draft numbers), SLA_addendum_v1.pdf

Can either of you review and flag any redlines? If we agree, I'll send to Alex + procurement and propose a 1-week signature target.

Thanks — Camila

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal check-in + usage questions — proposed offer and needs

Camila — this looks reasonable. My notes:
- Approve 20% uplift commit + 10% volume discount.
- Approve 3 months of 100k burst credits, but conditional on committing to a 12-mo term.
- Approve a one-time 20k token sign-on credit as a sweetener (not stackable with other promos).

Ben — please sanity-check the Dedicated sizing and add an ops note on autoscaling guardrails (we should ensure they can't blow past cost without alerting).

I updated the proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx with the adjusted economics and added a line item for the sign-on credit.

-Marissa
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference

Subject: Renewal proposal: capacity + SLA addendum (draft)

Alex — thanks again for the quick sync last week. Per our conversation, attaching a short proposal:

- Term: 12 months (auto-renew opt-out)
- Commit: 21.6M tokens/month (20% uplift over current run-rate)
- Pricing: 10% discount on committed token consumption, normal overage rates apply to consumption above commit; 100k burst credits/month for first 3 months; one-time 20k token sign-on credit applied at invoice 1.
- Low-latency routing: allocate Dedicated priority pool (estimated 2x T4 equivalent) for the 3 named routes (Assist-main, Assist-fallback, Search-index) with latency SLOs captured in SLA_addendum_v1.pdf.

Attachments: redwood_usage_q1-q2_2028.csv; SLA_addendum_v1.pdf; proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx

Next steps: if procurement is aligned we can circulate a DocuSign for the term sheet and SLA, or I can push a HubSpot quote (link below). Please confirm by end of day 2028-05-12 to secure the burst credits and current pricing.

HubSpot quote: https://hubspot.example/deal/CW-2028-RNW1
